fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

fields.name: customer_id
fields.short: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI.

fields.name: customer_identifiers
fields.short: Identifiers for the person in a response—`id`, `cio_id`, and `email`.

fields.name: deduplicate_id
fields.short: An identifier in the format `id:timestamp` where the id is for the object you're working with (Automations, Deliveries, Exports, Identities, One-time sends, Segments, and Templates), and the timestamp is the last time the object was update…

fields.name: end
fields.short: The end of the window we reported on, in ISO 8601 format.

fields.name: exited_early
fields.short: People who started a journey but stopped meeting the automation trigger/filter criteria.

fields.name: failure_message
fields.short: Explains why a message failed, if applicable.

fields.name: finished
fields.short: People who finished the journey.

fields.name: forgotten
fields.short: If true message contents are not retained by Customer.io.

fields.name: id
fields.short: The identifier for a delivery—the instance of a message intended for an individual recipient.

fields.name: language_variants
fields.short: Metrics for each language variant of a multi-language message, keyed by the variant's action ID.

fields.name: message_template_id
fields.short: The identifier of the message template used to create a message.

fields.name: messaged
fields.short: People who experienced at least one non-delay action in the journey.

fields.name: metric
fields.short: Contains metrics for the link.

fields.name: metrics
fields.short: Metrics for an individual instance of a message; each item in the object represents the timestamp when a message achieved a particular metric.

fields.name: never_activated
fields.short: People who started a journey but were filtered out before they could experience any of the actions in the journey.

fields.name: next
fields.short: Indicates the next page of results.

fields.name: parent_action_id
fields.short: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

fields.name: recipient
fields.short: The recipient address for an action.

fields.name: res
fields.short: The resolution we reported at.

fields.name: series
fields.short: Metrics grouped by the requested resolution.

fields.name: start
fields.short: The start of the window we reported on, in ISO 8601 format.

fields.name: started
fields.short: The total number of people who meet the trigger criteria for a journey.

fields.name: subject
fields.short: The subject line for an `email` action.

fields.name: tracked_responses
fields.short: Tracked in-app survey responses, keyed by response option name.

fields.name: trigger_event_id
fields.short: The id of the event that triggered an event-triggered automation (not an API-triggered broadcast).

fields.name: type
fields.short: The type of message or action for a delivery, automation action, or related object.

fields.name: actions
fields.short: A list of actions used by the broadcast.

fields.name: active
fields.short: If true, the broadcast is active.

fields.name: broadcast_id
fields.short: The identifier for a broadcast.

fields.name: created
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

fields.name: created_at
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

fields.name: deduplicate_id
fields.short: An identifier in the format `id:timestamp` where the id is for the object you're working with (Automations, Deliveries, Exports, Identities, One-time sends, Segments, and Templates), and the timestamp is the last time the object was update…

fields.name: errors
fields.short: A list of errors in the format `line <x>: <error text>` to help you troubleshoot errors associated with your audience or data file.

fields.name: first_started
fields.short: The date and time when you activated the broadcast.

fields.name: id
fields.short: The identifier for a broadcast trigger.

fields.name: language_variants
fields.short: Metrics for each language variant of a multi-language message, keyed by the variant's action ID.

fields.name: metric
fields.short: Contains metrics for the link.

fields.name: msg_template_ids
fields.short: Indicates the message template(s) used in this broadcast.

fields.name: name
fields.short: The name of the broadcast.

fields.name: next
fields.short: The offset to pass as the `start` value to fetch the next page of errors.

fields.name: processed_at
fields.short: The date-time when Customer.io processed the trigger.

fields.name: state
fields.short: The state of the broadcast.

fields.name: tags
fields.short: An array of tags you set on this broadcast.

fields.name: type
fields.short: The type of broadcast.

fields.name: updated
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

fields.short: The `start` value for the next page of results.

fields.name: amp
fields.short: AMP HTML variant.

fields.name: available_languages
fields.short: List of [language codes](/journeys/channels/localization/attribute/#supported-languages) that reflect the languages this default email has been translated to.

fields.name: browser
fields.short: Browser used to render the client.

fields.name: category
fields.short: Where the client renders.

fields.name: check
fields.short: Which check produced this finding.

fields.name: client
fields.short: Name of the email client and device.

fields.name: client_ids
fields.short: The device identifiers requested for this job.

fields.name: content
fields.short: The content of your email.

fields.name: created
fields.short: Unix timestamp of when the translation was created.

fields.name: created_at
fields.short: When you submitted the preview job.

fields.name: created_on_publish
fields.short: `false` if you [saved the email](/integrations/api/app/tag/design-studio-emails/saveVersion/).

fields.name: credits_original
fields.short: Credits originally granted for a tier.

fields.name: credits_remaining
fields.short: Credits left to spend from this tier.

fields.name: description
fields.short: Explanatory text you provided when creating a version.

fields.name: details
fields.short: Explanation and suggested fix.

fields.name: envelope
fields.short: The envelope of your email, like from and to addresses.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.short: When this pool's credits expire, if ever.

fields.name: feedback
fields.short: `true` is you saved this version by creating a [round of feedback in Design Studio](/messaging/design-studio/collaboration/feedback/).

fields.name: has_unpublished_changes
fields.short: Indicates whether the email or any of its translations has content changes that haven't been published.

fields.name: html
fields.short: Full HTML with liquid tags left intact.

fields.name: id
fields.short: Unique identifier for the email.

fields.name: is_linked
fields.short: Whether the translation is linked to a workflow (automation, broadcast, etc)

fields.name: is_processed
fields.short: `true` once every device has settled, for the email in the path—a multi-language run reports each of its emails separately, so this doesn't reflect the whole run when it covers more than one.

fields.name: is_template
fields.short: Whether the translation is a template

fields.name: language
fields.short: The [language code](/journeys/channels/localization/attribute/#supported-languages) of the translation

fields.name: language_group_id
fields.short: ID of the parent email that groups all translations.

fields.name: lax_mode
fields.short: Set to `true` to render liquid variables missing from `sample_data` as blank instead of failing the job.

fields.name: name
fields.short: The batch label provided when you sent an email for previews.

fields.name: node
fields.short: The content and settings stored in the version.

fields.name: node_count
fields.short: How many email nodes the run covers—more than one for a multi-language run.

fields.name: node_id
fields.short: The UUID of the rendered email node.

fields.name: node_type
fields.short: Always `"EMAIL"`.

fields.name: os
fields.short: Operating system the client runs on.

fields.name: parent_folder_id
fields.short: UUID of the parent folder, or `null` if the email is in your root directory.

fields.name: previews
fields.short: One object per requested preview.

fields.name: replayed
fields.short: `true` when this call returned an existing run instead of starting a new one, and you weren't charged a second time for it.

fields.name: run_id
fields.short: ID of the preview job.

fields.name: sample_data
fields.short: Liquid variables to render with, as a JSON object—any shape is accepted, from flat variables like `{"first_name": "Janine"}` to nested ones like `{"customer": {"first_name": "Janine"}}`.

fields.name: severity
fields.short: Fix all errors to make sure your recipients get your email and you follow compliance requirements.

fields.name: state
fields.short: Whether this finding represents an issue.

fields.name: summary
fields.short: Location context, for example "In the email body".

fields.name: template_id
fields.short: The ID of the workflow template that received the content.

fields.name: text
fields.short: Plain text version of the email.

fields.name: tier
fields.short: The credit tier this pool belongs to.

fields.name: title
fields.short: Short human-readable title.

fields.name: total_previews_bounced
fields.short: Previews that produced no screenshot, whether the vendor bounced them or they failed on Customer.io's side.

fields.name: total_previews_cached
fields.short: Previews served from an earlier run's screenshot.

fields.name: total_previews_ready
fields.short: How many previews show a screenshot you can fetch, counted from the tiles themselves.

fields.name: total_previews_requested
fields.short: Previews requested in the job, for the email in the path.

fields.name: total_previews_succeeded
fields.short: Previews this run generated itself, excluding cached ones.

fields.name: transformers
fields.short: Automate repetitive actions like removing white space and inlining CSS with [transformers](/journeys/design-studio/emails/code-editor/overview/#transformers).

fields.name: updated
fields.short: Unix timestamp of the last update to the translation.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.short: When the job's status was last updated.

fields.name: version_id
fields.short: The identifier of the template version created by the publish.

fields.name: created_at
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

fields.name: deduplicate_id
fields.short: An identifier in the format `id:timestamp` where the id is for the object you're working with (Automations, Deliveries, Exports, Identities, One-time sends, Segments, and Templates), and the timestamp is the last time the object was update…

fields.name: description
fields.short: A description of the export.

fields.name: downloads
fields.short: Counts the total number of times the export has been downloaded.

fields.name: failed
fields.short: If true, the export was unsuccessful.

fields.name: id
fields.short: The identifier for the export.

fields.name: status
fields.short: The state of your export where `done` indicates an export that you can download, `pending`, indicates that your export is not ready to download, and `failed` indicates an export that has failed and will not be downloadable.

fields.name: total
fields.short: The number of entries in the export.

fields.name: type
fields.short: The type of information contained in the export.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

fields.name: user_email
fields.short: The email of the user who created the export.

fields.name: user_id
fields.short: The user who created the export.

fields.name: created_at
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

fields.name: data_to_process
fields.short: Controls whether your import adds and updates all rows, adds only new rows, or updates only existing rows.

fields.name: description
fields.short: A helpful description that can help you find and recognize your import operation.

fields.name: error
fields.short: If your import fails, this helps you understand why.

fields.name: id
fields.short: This is the `import_id` you'll use if you want to [lookup your import operation](/integrations/api/app/tag/imports/getImport/).

fields.name: identifier
fields.short: The type of identifier you used to identify people in your CSV.

fields.name: name
fields.short: A friendly name for your import.

fields.name: object_type_id
fields.short: The object type an object belongs to—like "Companies" or "Accounts".

fields.name: people_to_process
fields.short: Returned for people and event imports, even if you imported using the field `data_to_process`.

fields.name: rows_imported
fields.short: The number of rows we imported from the CSV.

fields.name: rows_to_import
fields.short: The total number of importable rows we found in the CSV.

fields.name: state
fields.short: The state of the import—whether your import is being processed, fully completed (`imported`), or if it failed.

fields.name: type
fields.short: The type of import.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

fields.name: action_id
fields.short: The identifier for an action.

fields.name: content_id
fields.short: The identifier for a message in a one-time send.

fields.name: created
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

fields.name: customer_id
fields.short: The ID of a customer profile, analogous to a "person" in the UI.

fields.name: customer_identifiers
fields.short: Identifiers for the person in a response—`id`, `cio_id`, and `email`.

fields.name: deduplicate_id
fields.short: An identifier in the format `id:timestamp` where the id is for the object you're working with (Automations, Deliveries, Exports, Identities, One-time sends, Segments, and Templates), and the timestamp is the last time the object was update…

fields.name: failure_message
fields.short: Explains why a message failed, if applicable.

fields.name: forgotten
fields.short: If true message contents are not retained by Customer.io.

fields.name: id
fields.short: The identifier for a delivery—the instance of a message intended for an individual recipient.

fields.name: message_template_id
fields.short: The identifier of the message template used to create a message.

fields.name: metrics
fields.short: Metrics for an individual instance of a message; each item in the object represents the timestamp when a message achieved a particular metric.

fields.name: parent_action_id
fields.short: The ID of the parent action, if the action occurred within an automation and has a parent (like a randomized split, etc).

fields.name: recipient
fields.short: The recipient address for an action.

fields.name: subject
fields.short: The subject line for an `email` action.

fields.name: tracked_responses
fields.short: Tracked in-app survey responses, keyed by response option name.

fields.name: trigger_event_id
fields.short: The id of the event that triggered an event-triggered automation (not an API-triggered broadcast).

fields.name: type
fields.short: The type of message or action for a delivery, automation action, or related object.

fields.short: A list of message variants in a one-time send, where a variant is a translation or A/B test.

fields.name: created

fields.name: deduplicate_id
fields.short: An identifier in the format `id:timestamp` where the id is for the object you're working with (Automations, Deliveries, Exports, Identities, One-time sends, Segments, and Templates), and the timestamp is the last time the object was update…

fields.name: name
fields.short: The name of the one-time send.

fields.name: recipient_segment_ids
fields.short: If the recipient conditions included segments, this returns a list of those segment ids.

fields.name: sent_at
fields.short: The last time the one-time send was sent.

fields.name: subscription_topic_id
fields.short: If you enabled a [subscription center](/journeys/channels/subscriptions/center/) on your workspace, this returns the id of the subscription preference you set.

fields.name: tags
fields.short: An array of tags associated with the one-time send.

fields.name: type
fields.short: Channel type for a one-time send or one-time send content variant.

fields.name: updated
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

fields.name: bcc
fields.short: The blind-copy address(es) for this action.

fields.name: body
fields.short: The body of the variant.

fields.name: body_amp
fields.short: AMP-enabled content for your email.

fields.name: cc
fields.short: The carbon-copy address(es) for this action.

fields.name: content_ids
fields.short: A list of message variants in a one-time send, where a variant is a translation or A/B test.

fields.name: created
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

fields.name: deduplicate_id
fields.short: An identifier in the format `id:timestamp` where the id is for the object you're working with (Automations, Deliveries, Exports, Identities, One-time sends, Segments, and Templates), and the timestamp is the last time the object was update…

fields.name: fake_bcc
fields.short: If true, rather than sending true copies to BCC addresses, Customer.io sends a copy of the message with the subject line containing the recipient address(es).

fields.name: from
fields.short: The address that the message is from, relevant if the action `type` is `email`.

fields.name: from_id
fields.short: The identifier of the `from` address, commonly known as the "sender".

fields.name: headers
fields.short: A JSON string containing header objects with `name` and `value`.

fields.name: id
fields.short: The identifier of a one-time send variant—a language in a multi-language one-time send or a test in an A/B test.

fields.name: language
fields.short: The language variant for your message.

fields.name: layout
fields.short: The layout used for the variant, if it exists.

fields.name: name
fields.short: The name of the variant, if it exists.

fields.name: newsletter_id
fields.short: The identifier for a one-time send.

fields.name: preheader_text
fields.short: [Also known as "preview text"](/journeys/channels/email/headers/custom-preheader-text/), this is the small block of text shown in an email inbox next to or underneath the subject line.

fields.name: preprocessor
fields.short: If CSS pre-processing is enabled, this key is populated with `premailer`.

fields.name: recipient
fields.short: The recipient address for an action.

fields.name: recipient_segment_ids
fields.short: If the recipient conditions included segments, this returns a list of those segment ids.

fields.name: reply_to
fields.short: The address that receives replies for the message, if applicable.

fields.name: reply_to_id
fields.short: The identifier for the `reply_to` address, if applicable.

fields.name: sent_at
fields.short: The last time the one-time send was sent.

fields.name: subject
fields.short: The subject line for an `email` action.

fields.name: subscription_topic_id
fields.short: If you enabled a [subscription center](/journeys/channels/subscriptions/center/) on your workspace, this returns the id of the subscription preference you set.

fields.name: tags
fields.short: An array of tags associated with the one-time send.

fields.name: type
fields.short: Channel type for a one-time send or one-time send content variant.

fields.name: updated
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

fields.name: disabled
fields.short: Set to `true` to quit sending events to the webhook URL.

fields.name: endpoint
fields.short: The webhook URL.

fields.name: events
fields.short: Specifies the types of events you want to report to your webhook.

fields.name: full_resolution
fields.short: Set to `false` to send unique open and click events to the webhook.

fields.name: id
fields.short: The identifier for the webhook.

fields.name: name
fields.short: The name of your webhook.

fields.name: type
fields.short: The type of webhook—`webhook` for a standard reporting webhook or `js` for a JavaScript webhook.

fields.name: with_content
fields.short: Set to `true` to include the message `body` in `_sent` events.

fields.name: attachments
fields.short: A dictionary of attachments where the filename is the key and the value is the base64-encoded contents.

fields.name: auto_create
fields.short: If `true` and your `transactional_message_id` doesn't match a record, Customer.io creates an empty record using that value as the *Trigger Name*.

fields.name: bcc
fields.short: Blind copy message recipients.

fields.name: body
fields.short: The HTML body of your message.

fields.name: body_amp
fields.short: AMP-enabled content for your email.

fields.name: body_plain
fields.short: The plaintext body of your message.

fields.name: cc
fields.short: Carbon copy message recipients, separated by commas.

fields.name: custom_data
fields.short: Optional key/value pairs you want to attach to the push payload.

fields.name: custom_device
fields.short: A device to perform an upsert operation at the time of send.

fields.name: custom_payload
fields.short: Optional key/value pairs you want to attach to the push payload.

fields.name: delivery_id
fields.short: A unique identifier for the message.

fields.name: disable_css_preprocessing
fields.short: Set to `true` to disable CSS preprocessing.

fields.name: disable_message_retention
fields.short: If true, the message body is not retained in delivery history.

fields.name: fake_bcc
fields.short: If true, rather than sending true copies to BCC addresses, Customer.io sends a copy of the message with the subject line containing the recipient address(es).

fields.name: from
fields.short: The address your email is from.

fields.name: headers
fields.short: A JSON string containing header objects with `name` and `value`.

fields.name: id
fields.short: The `trigger_id` for this operation.

fields.name: identifiers
fields.short: Identifies the person represented by your transactional message by one of, and only one of, `id`, `email`, or `cio_id`.

fields.name: image_url
fields.short: An image URL to show in the push.

fields.name: language
fields.short: Overrides language preferences for the person you want to send your transactional message to.

fields.name: link
fields.short: A deep link to open when the push is tapped.

fields.name: message
fields.short: The message body for your notification.

fields.name: message_data
fields.short: An object containing the key-value pairs referenced using liquid in your message.

fields.name: preheader
fields.short: Also known as "preview text", this is the block block of text that users see next to, or underneath, the subject line in their inbox.

fields.name: queue_draft
fields.short: If true, your transactional message is held as a draft in Customer.io and not sent directly to your audience.

fields.name: queued_at
fields.short: A Unix timestamp for when Customer.io accepted and queued your request.

fields.name: reply_to
fields.short: The address that recipients can reply to, if different from the `from` address.

fields.name: send_at
fields.short: For a scheduled message, the Unix timestamp when the message is set to send.

fields.name: send_to_unsubscribed
fields.short: If false, your message is not sent to unsubscribed recipients.

fields.name: sound
fields.short: **For iOS Only**: your notification can alert users with the device's default notification sound or play no sound at all.

fields.name: subject
fields.short: The subject line for your message.

fields.name: title
fields.short: The title for your notification.

fields.name: to
fields.short: The recipients you want to send to, separated by commas.

fields.name: tracked
fields.short: If true, Customer.io tracks opens and link clicks in your message.

fields.name: transactional_message_id
fields.short: The transactional message template you want to use.

fields.name: bcc
fields.short: The blind-copy address(es) for this action.

fields.name: body
fields.short: The body of the transactional message.

fields.name: body_amp
fields.short: AMP-enabled content for your email.

fields.name: cc
fields.short: The carbon-copy address(es) for this action.

fields.name: content
fields.short: The object represents a variant.

fields.name: created
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

fields.name: created_at
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was created.

fields.name: description
fields.short: A description of the transactional message.

fields.name: fake_bcc
fields.short: If true, rather than sending true copies to BCC addresses, Customer.io sends a copy of the message with the subject line containing the recipient address(es).

fields.name: from
fields.short: The address that the message is from, relevant if the action `type` is `email`.

fields.name: from_id
fields.short: The identifier of the `from` address, commonly known as the "sender".

fields.name: headers
fields.short: A JSON string containing header objects with `name` and `value`.

fields.name: hide_message_body
fields.short: If true, message contents are not retained in delivery history—you cannot recall the exact contents of the message.

fields.name: id
fields.short: The identifier for an action.

fields.name: language
fields.short: The language variant for your message.

fields.name: link_tracking
fields.short: If true, link tracking is enabled for this message.

fields.name: name
fields.short: The name of the transactional message.

fields.name: open_tracking
fields.short: If true, open-tracking is enabled for this message.

fields.name: preheader_text
fields.short: [Also known as "preview text"](/journeys/channels/email/headers/custom-preheader-text/), this is the small block of text shown in an email inbox next to or underneath the subject line.

fields.name: preprocessor
fields.short: If CSS pre-processing is enabled, this key is populated with `premailer`.

fields.name: queue_drafts
fields.short: If true, messages do not send automatically, and queue as drafts instead.

fields.name: recipient
fields.short: The recipient address for an action.

fields.name: reply_to
fields.short: The address that receives replies for the message, if applicable.

fields.name: reply_to_id
fields.short: The identifier for the `reply_to` address, if applicable.

fields.name: send_to_unsubscribed
fields.short: If true, people with an `unsubscribed` attribute set to `true` can trigger the message.

fields.name: subject
fields.short: The subject line for an `email` action.

fields.name: type
fields.short: The type of message.

fields.name: updated
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

fields.name: updated_at
fields.short: The date time when the referenced ID was last updated.

info.description: Our App API provides ways to trigger messages and retrieve information about people, automations, broadcasts, and more. # Overview The App API provides methods to send newsletters, transactional messages, and API-triggered broadcasts. You can create newsletters from scratch and update transactional messages and API-triggered broadcasts. For transactional messages and API-triggered broadcasts, your payload acts as a message "trigger" and can contain `data` that you reference in your messages using liquid—`{{trigger.}}`. The other endpoints help you retrieve information about people, segments, automations, broadcasts, etc; it also lets you update automation actions, messages, newsletter variants, etc. Aside from the [API-triggered broadcast](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/triggerBroadcast/) endpoint (1 per 10 seconds), requests are limited to 10 per second. [Transactional](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/sendEmail/) messages go through the same high-throughput ingress as our Track and Pipelines APIs and share their soft rate limit of 3000 requests per 3 seconds, which isn't strictly enforced. # We may add to these APIs As we release new features, we add endpoints and we may even add fields to existing endpoints. We don't announce these additions in advance. Fields we add will be backward compatible: existing fields keep their names and types. Build your integration to ignore fields it doesn't recognize. If you validate responses against a schema, make sure the schema accepts unknown keys. In JSON Schema, for example, don't set `additionalProperties: false`. # Use our Postman collection We've generated a Postman collection to help you get started with our APIs. If you fork this collection, you might want to disable the *Watch original collection* option. We automatically update our Postman collection whenever we release changes to our documentation, even if we don't change our APIs—which happens daily! Rather than being flooded with Postman notifications, you can check out our [Release Notes](/release-notes/) for updates to our APIs. **NOTE**: Postman endpoints default to our US APIs. If you're in our European (EU) region, you'll need to add `-eu` to the server variables (`track_api_url` and `app_api_url`). [](https://god.gw.postman.com/run-collection/23697545-2931c004-e63d-4cdc-bf4b-e685ba6da42d?action=collection%2Ffork&source=rip_markdown&collection-url=entityId%3D23697545-2931c004-e63d-4cdc-bf4b-e685ba6da42d%26entityType%3Dcollection%26workspaceId%3Db886877f-fc09-475f-84fe-6221a98f4d18#?env%5BCustomer.io%20API%20Environment%) # Server addresses: US and EU Customer.io hosts services in the United States (US) and European Union. Select the appropriate server address for your region. | Region | Server Address | | :-- | :-- | | US | https://api.customer.io | | EU | https://api-eu.customer.io | # Authentication All requests to the Customer.io App API use an [App API Key](#authentication). To authenticate, provide your key as a Bearer token in a HTTP Authorization header. You can create and manage your API keys—including keys with different scopes—in [your account settings page](https://fly.customer.io/settings/api_credentials?keyType=app). Each operation on this page references the authorization header it requires. # Rate Limits Most endpoints on this page are limited to 10 requests per second. The exceptions are: * [Transactional messages](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/sendEmail/) use the same soft rate limit of our Track and Pipelines APIs (3000 requests per 3 seconds, not strictly enforced). * The [API-triggered broadcast endpoint](/integrations/api/app/tag/send-messages/triggerBroadcast/) is limited to 1 request every 10 seconds. **Rate limits are subject to change. We may adjust these thresholds to ensure stable performance for all customers.**
